evals.name: discover-read-then-native-route
evals.prompt: A shared-repository owner must be asked for an integration window. Current runtime tool discovery has not yet returned. The executing agent proposes a single exec cell that prints ALL_TOOLS filtered by the current Codex namespace and immediately calls peer.py send. After the cell, discovery would show a native send_message_to_thread tool covering the exact known independent target. What should the agent do? No message has been sent; no installation or permission change is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Separate discovery from the dependent route decision, read the actual tool contract and target coverage, then use coord prepare -> the native tool with the exact prepared body -> coord commit. Do not preselect fallback, install a guard or grant mutation permission through a coordination reply.
expectations: Waits for and reads current discovery before choosing the sender; printing discovery and sending fallback in the same cell does not satisfy native-first
Uses the native tool when it covers the exact target, without also sending a script duplicate
Keeps coordination preparation and accepted/unknown/not_sent handling on the existing board contract
Makes no hook, receive-policy, service or authentication change

evals.name: accepted-fallback-is-not-replayed-after-discovery
evals.prompt: An agent prematurely used peer.py send while native discovery was still pending. The transport accepted the coordination, but receiver-side consumption is unverified. Discovery now returns a native tool covering that exact target. The user did not authorize a duplicate request. Describe recovery and the route for a future distinct coordination.
evals.expected_output: Retain the original message identity and accepted/unverified status, inspect its evidence through the applicable existing contract, and do not resend it through the newly discovered native tool. A future distinct coordination uses native prepare/send/commit after inspecting coverage.
expectations: Does not replay the same accepted or uncertain request through native transport
Distinguishes transport acceptance from consumption and business completion
Preserves the original message identity and does not delete queue state, resume a thread or change permissions
Uses native-first only for the future distinct request rather than retroactively duplicating this one

evals.name: antigravity-three-state-delivery-and-no-concurrent-resume
evals.prompt: A Claude Code session needs to send a coordination notice to an active Antigravity (agy) TUI conversation (`antigravity:a1b2c3d4-...`, listed as status=attached_tui). Should it use Claude's native SendMessage, force `peer.py send --antigravity-delivery resume`, or use default `peer.py send` (`auto`)? How does the live Antigravity TUI consume the message?
evals.expected_output: Do not call Claude SendMessage (blocked for antigravity: targets; do not run coord prepare either) and never force concurrent `agy -p` (`--antigravity-delivery resume`) against an attached_tui/running session (risks overwriting live .pb state). Send directly via `peer.py send antigravity:<uuid> ...` (default `auto` queues safely to the per-conversation durable inbox). The live TUI consumes it via `peer.py inbox` / `peer.py wait --inbox` (in a background task) or the optional user-installed Antigravity inbox hook.
expectations: Rejects Claude SendMessage and coord prepare for antigravity: targets
Forbids concurrent `agy -p` / `--antigravity-delivery resume` against attached_tui or running sessions
Uses direct `peer.py send` (`auto`/queued) into the durable per-conversation inbox
Explains receiver consumption via `peer.py inbox`, background `peer.py wait --inbox`, or opt-in hook without claiming unapproved hook installation

evals.name: one-command-reply-thread-and-no-courtesy-loop
evals.prompt: A peer receives (a) an open coordination request `msg-id: 9a8b7c6d-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` asking whether a branch is ready to merge, and later (b) a final notice saying 'Merged PR #42, no further action needed'. What CLI verbs should the peer use for (a) and (b)?
evals.expected_output: For (a), reply concisely with `peer.py reply 9a8b7c6d --message '...'` (or UTF-8 file / `-` stdin), which resolves the sender/topic, propagates `thread_id`, and auto-closes the parent request on accepted delivery. For (b), do not send a courtesy 'received/acknowledged' reply that restarts a loop; close it quietly via `peer.py coord receive <file> --disposition no-reply` (or end the turn quietly if no action is needed).
expectations: Uses `peer.py reply <id-or-8hex>` for the open request instead of hand-assembling 6 `send` flags
Notes `thread_id` propagation and automatic parent closure on `accepted` delivery
Refuses to send a courtesy-only echo for the completion notice (anti-courtesy-loop)
Uses `coord receive --disposition no-reply` (or quiet completion) for non-request completion notices

evals.name: event-driven-wait-and-idle-tui-wakeup
evals.prompt: An Antigravity session sends a blocking question to a Codex peer and wants to wait up to 5 minutes for a reply without burning tokens in a `sleep`/polling loop, and wants its own idle TUI to wake up immediately when the reply arrives. What command pattern should it use and what does exit code 11 mean?
evals.expected_output: Use `peer.py wait --message-id <id> --timeout 300 --json` (or `peer.py send ... --wait-reply 300` / background `peer.py wait --inbox --timeout 300 --json` launched via the host's async background task runner so the main turn can finish with 0 tokens burned while OS `kqueue` watches for arrival). Exit code 11 means the bounded timeout elapsed with `status="timeout"`, `checked_sources`, and a `next_command` — do not loop endlessly.
expectations: Uses `peer.py wait` (`--message-id` or `--inbox`) or `--wait-reply` instead of shell `sleep` polling
Pairs `wait` with host background task execution for zero-token idle-TUI wakeup
Correctly interprets exit code 11 as bounded timeout (not transport failure) and respects the bounded window without infinite retries

evals.name: unified-inbox-cursors-and-short-prefix-ambiguity
evals.prompt: A Claude session checks unread peer messages with `peer.py inbox --json` and marks them read with `--ack`. Does `--ack` mutate Claude's JSONL transcript or Codex's SQLite queue? Separately, what happens if two targets share the 8-hex prefix `a1b2c3d4`?
evals.expected_output: `peer.py inbox --ack` never mutates Claude transcripts or Codex SQLite; it writes per-session read cursors under `<state-dir>/inbox-cursors/` (locked atomically). When a `>=8`-hex prefix matches multiple sessions, the CLI fails closed (exit 3) and lists all colliding full addresses instead of guessing.
expectations: States clearly that `inbox --ack` only updates `<state-dir>/inbox-cursors/` and never mutates Claude transcripts or Codex SQLite
States that ambiguous `>=8`-hex prefixes fail closed (exit 3) listing colliding candidates
Never guesses a target by recency or title when a prefix collides

evals.name: soft-lease-expired-unreleased-and-retired-network-redirect
evals.prompt: An agent runs `peer.py coord start --repo . --path 'src/*.py' --task fix-auth --actor codex:<uuid>` and receives `status="conflict"` where the active owner has `freshness="expired_unreleased"`. Can the agent silently take over the files? Also, a user asks how to set up cross-machine `peer-message:v1` pairing across two laptops.
evals.expected_output: No — `expired_unreleased` is advisory staleness, never automatic takeover; the agent must verify actual git/file state or contact the recorded owner (using `next_command`), and only the recorded owner may `coord renew` or `coord release`. For cross-machine or cross-user messaging, explain that the old `peer-message` network preview is retired and direct the user to Agent Use (`https://useagent.app`).
expectations: Enforces `staleness != takeover`: refuses silent takeover on `expired_unreleased`
Explains that only the recorded owner can `coord renew` or `coord release`, while the newcomer verifies actual sources or contacts the owner
States that the cross-machine `network` preview is retired and redirects to Agent Use (`https://useagent.app`)
